PARAMETRIC ILLUSTRATION · NOT RESEARCH GEOMETRY

01 / THE PROBLEM

Start from the goal,
not the geometry.

Inverse design flips the usual question. Instead of simulating a shape someone drew, the AI is asked to generate the shape that meets the goal. My PhD tests this on wind turbine blades.

02 / THE REPRESENTATION

A shape a model
can reason about.

Beneath the surface, the blade becomes a compact parameter vector: airfoil sections, spanwise chord, and twist. This is the representation the learning system generates and optimises.

03 / THE CONSTRAINTS

Physics as
a learning signal.

BEM constraints, icing, and site conditions are built into the model itself, so generated designs are plausible before they reach CFD. Fully automated, end to end.

WHAT THE MODEL DESIGNS

Three layers.
One structure, generated by AI.

INSET-FED RECTANGULAR PATCH · NOT TO SCALE
  1. 01

    Patch & feed · model output

    The cascade predicts patch dimensions, inset feed parameters, and input impedance from a target frequency.

  2. 02

    Substrate · model input

    Material properties condition every prediction. The dataset spans six substrate materials and 24 physical descriptors.

  3. 03

    Ground plane · fixed structure

    Completes the design that CST simulation uses to cross-validate the model’s predictions.

03 / THE PERSON BEHIND THE MODELS

From computer systems
to applied intelligence.

ws.

ALGERIA → HUNGARY
COMPUTER SYSTEMS → APPLIED AI

AI / ML engineer.
Researcher. System builder.

I’m an AI PhD researcher at the Doctoral School of Informatics at Eötvös Loránd University in Budapest, working under Prof. László Kollár. I’m building EACID, a physics-informed cascade ML framework that designs wind turbine blades end to end, with no human in the loop.

My core expertise is data-efficient inverse design, physics-constrained neural networks, and applied deep learning. The domain is the variable: aerodynamics, electromagnetics, wireless networks, or enterprise software. I frame each one as a learning problem and own the whole path, from dataset to model to a tool people can use. Before ELTE, I studied Computer & Systems Engineering at École nationale polytechnique Maurice Audin and built AI applications for satellite systems at the Algerian Space Agency’s CDS.
